question: Which of the following best describes an uncomplicated urinary tract infection?

options.A: An infection occurring in a patient with an indwelling urinary catheter
options.B: An infection occurring in a healthy, non-pregnant woman with a normal urinary tract
options.C: An infection that has ascended to cause severe pyelonephritis
options.D: An infection secondary to a structural urinary tract abnormality

explanation: Uncomplicated UTIs typically occur in healthy, non-pregnant women who have no structural or functional abnormalities of the urinary tract. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T2#GNS223_U8_T2_h1)

question: What is a primary host defense mechanism against urinary tract infections?

options.B: Frequent and regular flushing action of micturition
options.C: Complete absence of resident mucosal flora
options.D: High concentration of systemic red blood cells

explanation: The mechanical flushing action of micturition helps wash away invading pathogens before they can colonize the urinary tract. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T2#GNS223_U8_T2_h1)

question: Which bacterial pathogen is responsible for the vast majority of community-acquired urinary tract infections?
explanation: Uropathogenic Escherichia coli (UPEC) accounts for the vast majority of community-acquired urinary tract infections. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T2#GNS223_U8_T2_h2)

question: Which organism is frequently associated with urinary tract infections in young, sexually active females?
explanation: Staphylococcus saprophyticus is a common Gram-positive bacterium known to cause urinary tract infections specifically in young, sexually active females. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T2#GNS223_U8_T2_h2)

question: What is the primary mechanism of action of fluoroquinolones like ciprofloxacin?

options.A: Inhibition of bacterial cell wall synthesis
options.B: Inhibition of bacterial DNA synthesis via DNA gyrase
options.C: Irreversible binding to the 30S ribosomal subunit

explanation: Fluoroquinolones inhibit bacterial DNA synthesis by targeting bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV enzymes. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T2#GNS223_U8_T2_h3)

question: Why is nitrofurantoin unique and primarily used for lower urinary tract infections?

options.A: It concentrates heavily in renal tissue and blood serum for systemic infections
options.B: It damages bacterial DNA and concentrates effectively in the urine
options.C: It acts exclusively against fungal pathogens in the bladder
options.D: It stimulates host immune cell production in the kidneys

explanation: Nitrofurantoin works by damaging bacterial DNA through reactive intermediates and is uniquely concentrated within the urinary tract, making it ideal for lower UTIs. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T2#GNS223_U8_T2_h3)

question: Which of the following is commonly recommended as a first-line oral treatment for uncomplicated acute cystitis?

options.C: Oral ciprofloxacin as primary first-line routine

explanation: Oral nitrofurantoin is a standard first-line agent for uncomplicated lower UTIs due to its targeted urinary concentration and favorable safety profile. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T2#GNS223_U8_T2_h4)

question: Why are fluoroquinolones generally discouraged as initial first-line routine agents for uncomplicated UTIs?

options.A: They have zero activity against gram-negative bacteria
options.B: Concerns regarding adverse effects and promotion of antimicrobial resistance
options.C: They can only be administered via continuous intravenous infusion
options.D: They turn the urine a harmless brown color

explanation: Fluoroquinolones are reserved due to adverse effect profiles and the critical need to preserve their efficacy by preventing widespread resistance. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T2#GNS223_U8_T2_h4)

question: What distinguishes complicated UTIs from uncomplicated UTIs in terms of initial management and treatment?

options.A: Complicated UTIs require shorter single-dose therapies
options.B: Complicated UTIs require culture collection, broader initial agents, and longer treatment durations
options.C: Complicated UTIs can always be managed effectively with home oral nitrofurantoin
options.D: Complicated UTIs never require hospitalization or intravenous therapy

explanation: Complicated UTIs carry higher risks and require cultures, broader initial antimicrobial coverage, and longer courses of therapy (7 to 14 days or more). [learn more](GNS223_U8_T2#GNS223_U8_T2_h5)

question: Why is culturing urine and blood important before starting therapy for suspected pyelonephritis?

options.A: To prove that the patient has no bacterial pathogens present
options.B: To allow for targeted de-escalation of therapy once sensitivities are known
options.C: To ensure the patient receives lifelong prophylactic antibiotics
options.D: To eliminate the need for any antibiotic administration

explanation: Cultures allow clinicians to identify the exact causative organism and its sensitivities, enabling safe de-escalation from broad to narrow-spectrum therapy. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T2#GNS223_U8_T2_h5)

question: What is the standard empirical combination therapy often used to treat suspected gonococcal urethritis due to frequent co-infection?

options.A: Intramuscular ceftriaxone plus oral azithromycin or doxycycline
options.B: Oral nitrofurantoin alone for three days

explanation: Ceftriaxone combined with azithromycin or doxycycline is standard to effectively cover both Neisseria gonorrhoeae and co-infecting Chlamydia trachomatis. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T2#GNS223_U8_T2_h6)

question: Why is partner treatment an essential component of managing sexually transmitted genito-urinary infections?

options.A: To increase hospital revenue and medication sales
options.B: To prevent immediate reinfection of the index patient
options.C: To eliminate the need for laboratory testing in all cases
options.D: To shorten the incubation period of the pathogen

explanation: Treating sexual partners concurrently prevents ping-pong transmission and reinfection of the primary patient. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T2#GNS223_U8_T2_h6)

question: Which of the following practices significantly contributes to rising antibiotic resistance patterns in Nigeria?

options.A: Strict adherence to prescription-only antibiotic policies
options.B: Over-the-counter purchase and incomplete courses of antibiotics
options.C: Routine laboratory culture and sensitivity testing before treatment
options.D: De-escalating broad-spectrum antibiotics based on sensitivity reports

explanation: Purchasing antibiotics without prescriptions and failing to complete prescribed courses select for resistant bacterial strains, fueling the resistance crisis. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T2#GNS223_U8_T2_h7)

question: What does the emergence of ESBL-producing uropathogens imply for clinicians?

options.A: Standard penicillins and cephalosporins will be reliably effective
options.B: Infections can be treated successfully with topical antifungal creams
options.C: Standard penicillins and cephalosporins are rendered ineffective, requiring alternative agents
options.D: Bacteria have become completely eradicated from the urinary tract

explanation: Extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) production destroys many standard penicillins and cephalosporins, rendering them ineffective. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T2#GNS223_U8_T2_h7)

question: What is a key nursing intervention in preventing catheter-associated urinary tract infections (CAUTIs)?

options.A: Disconnecting the catheter tubing frequently to check urine flow
options.B: Maintaining a closed sterile drainage system and prompt catheter removal when indicated
options.C: Elevating the urine collection bag above the level of the patient's bladder
options.D: Administering prophylactic intravenous vancomycin to all catheterized patients

explanation: Maintaining a closed sterile drainage system and removing unnecessary catheters promptly are core evidence-based interventions for preventing CAUTIs. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T2#GNS223_U8_T2_h8)

question: What vital instruction should a nurse give to a patient prescribed a 7-day course of antibiotics for a urinary tract infection?

options.A: Stop taking the medication as soon as burning symptoms disappear on day two
options.B: Double the dose if a single dose is missed to speed up recovery
options.C: Complete the full course of antibiotics even if symptoms resolve completely
options.D: Restrict daily fluid intake to prevent frequent urination

explanation: Patients must complete the entire course of antibiotics to ensure complete eradication of the pathogen and prevent recurrence or resistance development. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T2#GNS223_U8_T2_h8)
